result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_planar()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph is planar. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L4461-L4543){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_planar() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A planar graph can be embedded in a plane without any edge crossings. This method uses Euler's formula and necessary conditions to test planarity. For simple planar graphs with `n ≥ 3` nodes, the number of edges *e* must satisfy `e ≤ 3n - 6`. For graphs without triangles, the stricter bound *e* ≤ *2n - 4* applies. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the graph satisfies planarity conditions, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} This is a *necessary but not sufficient* test. Some non-planar graphs may pass this test. For complete planarity testing, specialized algorithms implementing Kuratowski's theorem would be required. However, this test will correctly identify many non-planar graphs efficiently. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Small graphs are typically planar: ::: {#f73121f9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # Returns True graph.is_planar() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: The complete graph K_4 is planar: ::: {#d29a9ef3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(n=4) # Returns True (4 nodes, 6 edges: 6 ≤ 3 * 4 - 6 = 6) graph.is_planar() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Complete graph K_5 is not planar: ::: {#95ce9c93 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(n=5) # Returns False (5 nodes, 10 edges: 10 > 3 * 5 - 6 = 9) graph.is_planar() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Trees are always planar: ::: {#38c2e5f4 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = ec.Graph(directed=False) tree.add_balanced_tree(k=3, h=4) # Returns True (trees have `e = n - 1`) tree.is_planar() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Grid graphs are planar: ::: {#97ac515d .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} grid = ec.Graph(directed=False) grid.add_grid_2d(rows=5, cols=5) # Returns True grid.is_planar() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` True ``` ::: :::
